links.comparator_used: Standard prompt without mitigation instructions under biased consultations
links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy under patient cognitive bias
links.effect: Limited and inconsistent improvements; did not reliably prevent bias-induced performance loss (bias-induced declines were approximately 7 to 39 percentage points)
links.quote: Prompt-based mitigation strategies and decoding temperature reduction yielded limited and inconsistent improvements and did not reliably prevent bias-induced performance loss.

links.comparator_used: Default or higher decoding temperature settings (4 temperature settings tested)
links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy under patient cognitive bias
links.effect: Limited and inconsistent improvements; did not reliably prevent bias-induced performance loss
links.quote: Prompt-based mitigation strategies and decoding temperature reduction yielded limited and inconsistent improvements and did not reliably prevent bias-induced performance loss.

links.comparator_used: Foundation-only condition, where the same LLM performed both interaction and diagnosis
links.effect: Gains of approximately 10 to 39 percentage points across most models, recovering a large proportion of performance lost due to bias, particularly in lower-capacity systems
links.quote: By contrast, the dual-system framework substantially improved diagnostic accuracy under biased conditions, producing gains of approximately 10 to 39 percentage points across most models and recovering a large proportion of the performance lost due to bias, particularly in lower-capacity systems.

links.comparator_used: Foundation conversational LLM performing both interaction and final diagnosis
links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy under biased consultations when a reasoning-oriented LLM (o1-mini) made the final diagnosis
links.effect: Gains of approximately 10 to 39 percentage points across most models
links.quote: By contrast, the dual-system framework substantially improved diagnostic accuracy under biased conditions, producing gains of approximately 10 to 39 percentage points across most models and recovering a large proportion of the performance lost due to bias, particularly in lower-capacity systems.
